audit.summary: The real Gaussian mass estimate in (5.2) has the wrong exponent; the exact-zero5/4 deduction can be repaired. The graph transform loses isolated-vertex mass, with explicit modular examples at arbitrarily large N. A continuous unbounded density disproves the general uniform transfer rate. The Eisenstein scaling remains a named unresolved input.
limitations: P001 — The one-dimensional Gaussian mass in (5.2) is incorrectly bounded by the square of the interval radius — Counterevidence: The direct exact-zero argument recovers Theorem 1.3's 5/4 exponent. The qualitative cusp-form result uses only o(1) small/large-period probabilities and is not undermined by this squared-radius mistake. No actual Maaß form or geodesic family contradicting the stronger theorem has been produced.

P002 — The actual graph transform is not automatically a probability measure — Counterevidence: A positive mass for each finiteN does not imply positive limiting mass. No asymptotic counterexample to Theorem1.9 is asserted. The unweighted §5 edge-count proof does not require normalization and ignores isolated vertices.

P003 — Continuity of a density does not imply the uniform O(E) endpoint estimate — Counterevidence: The standard Gaussian is bounded, so a bounded-density correction works for the intended Gaussian input. It does not repair the separate isolated-mass issue.

Limits: This contribution does not certify the exact equality (4.6), the two-sided error claimed in Lemma 4.1, or non-isolation of X_N. In particular, isolated vertices contribute zero to these degree sums and do not obstruct this one-sided argument.

Limits: This is not a claim that every literal representative/sign sentence in the printed proof is exact. The argument only requires an absolute constant. Primitive axes and the stated cusp embedding remain part of the source setup.
Limits: The Aka–Einsiedler theorem, full prime-geodesic equidistribution, geodesic-flow ergodicity and class-number/counting results are declared dependencies.

Limits: No counterexample to the truth of Theorem 5.1 is claimed. The weaker small-period estimate and the exact-zero repair are new analytic deductions in this bounded contribution, not independent acceptance of the paper.
Limits: The Eisenstein case is excluded from this positive conclusion because its displayed normalizing factors are inconsistent in the source and require separate resolution.

proposition.claim:
Theorem5.1's stated exponent is obtained by (5.2)'s squared-radius Gaussian estimate.

Real one-dimensional Maaß-period Gaussian input of Theorem3.4, uniform interval error O((log N)^(-1/2)). delta>0; alpha=1+min(delta,1/4); comparison error O(1) along edges.

For any probability measure mu on X, the specified G(mu) has total mass1 and mu(e^-1(B))≤G(mu)(B).

I={x:deg(x)=0}; e^-1(B) includes all vertices whose entire neighbour set is contained in B, including empty sets. The actual graph has X_N double cosets with0<c≤N and Y_N classes with N/2≤absolute trace≤N; mu_N is uniform on X_N.

For every continuous probability densityF the interval comparison is uniformly O_F(h(n)+E(n)).

F(x)=sum_(j≥1) j(1−|x−3j|/w_j)_+, w_j=2^(−j)/j. Disjoint triangular spikes give a locally finite continuous density with total integral sum2^(−j)=1 and unbounded heights. For eachn choose a finite midpoint-quantile approximation with uniform interval errorh(n)≤w_n². Take a matching graph between two copies, f_n equal to quantiles andg_n=f_n+w_n.

repair.content:
Correct (5.2) and revise the quantitative small-period bound to the checked exponent, or supply a new argument establishing the stronger exponent. For δ≥1/2 retain the O(1) comparison term rather than absorbing it into a decaying threshold.

Require mu(I)=0 for the abstract lemma. For the actual graph, condition on nonisolated vertices or change the construction, and establish the necessary isolated-mass estimate. The distributional comparison then includes O(zeta_N) for zeta_N=mu_N(I_N).

Assume F is bounded, or replaceO(E) by the uniform concentration modulus sup_b integral_b^(b+O(E))F. The latter tends to0 for integrableF, but need not beO(E).
